scenario.title: Wafer Sample Transfer and Disposal Request
scenario.initial_description: Samples are moved when they are needed for evaluation. After evaluation, unnecessary samples are checked and disposed of through a request process.

reference_workflow.goal: Move required wafer samples for evaluation and dispose of completed samples through traceable approval.

activities.name: Identify required sample and evaluation purpose
Submit disposal request for completed sample

decisions.condition: Is the sample available and correctly identified?

automation_opportunities.rationale: Transfer request fields can be pre-filled from sample identifiers and evaluation purpose.
Status updates can be prompted automatically after scheduled evaluation completion.
Disposal candidates can be suggested when retention conditions are not met.

activities.name: Transport Wafer Sample to Evaluation Area
Review Evaluation Results and Classify Sample
Update Sample Inventory and Close Request

decisions.condition: Is the wafer sample needed for further evaluation or future use?
Is the disposal request approved by Lab Manager / EHS Officer?

exceptions.description: Wafer sample not found in storage at expected location
exceptions.handling: Escalate to Lab Manager; conduct inventory audit; suspend transfer request until resolved

exceptions.trigger: Physical damage detected during A4 or A5
exceptions.handling: Document damage; notify Process Engineer; determine if evaluation can proceed or sample must be disposed immediately

exceptions.description: Disposal request rejected due to non-compliance or insufficient documentation
exceptions.handling: Return to requester with rejection reason; requester revises and resubmits disposal request

exceptions.description: Regulatory or EHS constraint prevents standard disposal method
exceptions.trigger: Special material classification identified during A8 or A9
exceptions.handling: Route to EHS Officer for special handling procedure; engage certified disposal vendor if required

automation_opportunities.target: A1 - Identify Wafer Sample Transfer Need
automation_opportunities.rationale: Transfer needs can be automatically triggered by evaluation scheduling systems when a new evaluation request is logged, eliminating manual identification steps.
constraints: requires integration between evaluation scheduling and sample management systems
automated triggers must handle priority overrides

automation_opportunities.rationale: Transfer requests with standard parameters (known sample, known destination, standard urgency) can be auto-generated and routed without manual initiation.
constraints: non-standard or high-value samples may still require manual review
access control rules must be encoded

automation_opportunities.target: A3 - Retrieve Wafer Sample from Storage
automation_opportunities.rationale: In facilities with automated storage and retrieval systems (ASRS), sample retrieval can be fully automated based on the approved transfer order.
constraints: requires physical automation infrastructure (ASRS or robotic handlers)
manual fallback needed for exception cases

automation_opportunities.rationale: Certain evaluation steps (dimensional measurement, defect scanning) can be automated using metrology tools integrated with the evaluation system.
constraints: not all evaluation types are automatable; some require human judgment
equipment calibration must be maintained

automation_opportunities.target: D1 - Is the wafer sample needed for further use?
automation_opportunities.rationale: Classification rules based on evaluation outcome scores, sample age, and predefined retention policies can automate the retain/dispose decision for clear-cut cases.
constraints: borderline or ambiguous cases must be escalated to human review
policy rules must be kept current

automation_opportunities.rationale: When the dispose decision is made, disposal request forms can be auto-populated using sample metadata, classification, and applicable disposal method from policy rules.
constraints: special material categories may require manual annotation
regulatory fields must be validated before submission

automation_opportunities.target: A9 - Review and Approve Disposal Request
automation_opportunities.rationale: Routine disposal requests meeting standard criteria (material type, quantity thresholds, standard disposal method) can be auto-approved via rule-based workflow.
constraints: hazardous or regulated materials must always require human approval
audit trail must be preserved for all auto-approvals

automation_opportunities.target: A11 - Update Sample Inventory and Close Request
automation_opportunities.rationale: Upon receipt of disposal certificate or confirmation, inventory records can be automatically updated and the request automatically closed without manual data entry.
constraints: requires reliable disposal confirmation signal from EHS system
data integrity checks must be in place

assumptions: Wafer samples are physical semiconductor wafer specimens used for quality evaluation and process verification purposes.
A sample management system exists to track sample identities, locations, and statuses.
An EHS (Environmental Health and Safety) system or equivalent is used to manage disposal compliance and documentation.
Sample transfer occurs within the same facility or between nearby facility areas; long-distance logistics are not considered in scope.
Evaluation is performed in a designated lab or metrology area by qualified personnel.
Disposal is subject to regulatory or internal EHS requirements and requires formal approval before execution.
Samples classified as 'retain' are returned to storage for potential future use.
Multiple samples may be involved in a single transfer or disposal batch, but the workflow is modeled at the individual sample level.
Automated storage and retrieval infrastructure may not be present in all implementations; automation confidence for A3 reflects this uncertainty.
The disposal process assumes at least a two-level approval hierarchy (requester + approver) for compliance purposes.
